parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the electric field strength.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the magnitude and the sign of the charge on the oil drop.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The electric potentials of the plates are instantaneously reversed so that the top plate is at a potential of $0\text{ V}$ and the bottom plate is at a potential of $+1340\text{ V}$. This change causes the oil drop to start moving downwards.
parts.text: Compare the new pattern of the electric field lines between the plates with the original pattern.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the oil drop.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of the acceleration of the oil drop is $20\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Assume that the radius of the oil drop is negligible.

Use the information in (b)(iii) to calculate the time taken for the oil drop to move to the bottom metal plate from its initial position mid-way between the plates.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The oil drop in (b) starts to move at time $t = 0$. The distance of the oil drop from the bottom plate is $x$.

On Fig. 2.2, sketch the variation with time $t$ of distance $x$ for the movement of the drop from its initial position until it hits the surface of the bottom plate. Numerical values of $t$ are not required.

stem:
A charged oil drop is in a vacuum between two horizontal metal plates. A uniform electric field is produced between the plates by applying a potential difference of $1340\text{ V}$ across them, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

Fig. 2.1

The separation of the plates is $1.4 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}$.

The oil drop of weight $4.6 \times 10^{-14}\text{ N}$ remains stationary at a point mid-way between the plates.
